neighbours.label: the slot just before an expected word of intricacy or sophistication: comparative ' more' / ' most' (or a word-start like ' es'-oteric) where 'sophisticated / profound / intricate / subtle' is predicted next
fire: As the years passed, the techniques of forgers became more sophisticated.
The exhibits range from the crudest stone tools to the most refined jewellery.
Each generation of hackers has developed tools that are more sophisticated than the last.
His lectures move from the plainest facts to the most profound questions.
He wrote his thesis on a rather esoteric branch of number theory.
With time, the cheating schemes in the casino grew more elaborate.
Her designs go from the simple and plain to the most intricate lacework.
Since then the tricks of smugglers have become more subtle.
quiet: As the years passed, the houses in the valley became more expensive.
The exhibits range from the oldest stone tools to the most recent jewellery.
Each generation of farmers has planted fields that are more dry than the last.
His lectures move from the morning session to the most crowded evening one.
He wrote his thesis on a rather early period of Roman history.
With time, the winters in the mountains grew more cold.
Her trips go from the short and cheap to the most distant islands.
Since then the visits of his cousins have become more rare.

notes: Card: peaks on 'the simplest to the ⟦most⟧ profound', 'become ⟦more⟧ sophisticated', '⟦ es⟧oteric', '⟦ Intr⟧icate'; the - pole promotes subt/intricate/refined/nuanced/complex. Probes: 'methods of fraud have become more' 0.73 (same whatever follows: a prediction), 'the simplest to the most' 0.46, 'rather es|oteric' 0.43, 'far more elaborate' 0.33; 'most complicated movements' 0.12, 'most expensive' 0.04-0.07.
